# Part 2 – Technical-Functional Layout

## Benchmark of the Movie Information API


Three movie data APIs are under consideration for the project: IMDb, OMDb, and TMDB. The goal is to compare them, rule out any unsuitable options, and select the one that provides the most relevant information based on the transmitted JSON (e.g., searching for information on the movie "The Odyssey").

# Comparison of the Three APIs {.unlisted .unnumbered}

| Criteria | OMDb | TMDB | IMDb |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Price | Free (1000 req./day) | Free (40 req./10s) or paid upon negotiation | Paid (AWS, min. $150,000) |
| Official Public API | Yes | Yes | No |
| Ease of Use | Easy | Easy | Difficult (AWS) |
| Data Completeness | Complete | Very complete | Very complete |
| License | Commercial use allowed | Non-commercial use by default | Mandatory commercial license |
| Language | English only | French supported (fr-FR) | French supported |

# Exclusion of IMDb {.unlisted .unnumbered}

IMDb ruled out:
No official public API available: access is provided via AWS with a minimum entry cost of $150,000. Incompatible with the our plan to build an app. The following evaluation therefore focuses solely on OMDb and TMDB.

# OMDb vs TMDB — JSON Comparison {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Based on the same search query ("The Odyssey"), here is the relevant data returned by each API:

| Data Field | OMDb (JSON) | TMDB (JSON, language=fr-FR) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Title | `"Title": "The Odyssey"`<br>*(English only)* | `"title": "L'Odyssée"`<br>*(Translated into French)* |
| Synopsis | `"Plot"` in English only<br>*"After the Trojan War..."* | `"overview"` translated into French<br>*"Vingt ans après son départ..."* |
| Genres | `"Genre": "Action, Adventure, Fantasy"`<br>*(English text)* | `"genres": [{"id_genre": "Aventure"}, ...]`<br>*(Translated)* |
| Runtime | `"Runtime": "172 min"` | `"runtime": 173`<br>*(minutes)* |
| Release Date | `"Released": "17 Jul 2026"` | `"release_date": "2026-07-15"` |
| Content Rating | `'Rated': 'R'`<br>*(US age rating classification)* | `"adult": False`<br>*(Indicates if the movie is rated adult/pornographic)*<br><br>`"softcore": False`<br>*(Specific flag designating non-explicit erotic content)* |

## Final Decision {.unlisted .unnumbered}

TMDB is selected: It is the only candidate among the two to return key fields such as title, synopsis, and genres translated into French (via the language=fr-FR parameter), whereas OMDb strictly provides these fields in English.


# Accounting Module 

The Accounting Module collects sales data and tracks financial performance. This report presents the main accounting and analytics features chosen for the system.

## Key Indicators {.unlisted .unnumbered}

* **Number of Tickets Sold:** Shows the total volume of sales. This number measures attendance and is used for official ticketing reports.
* **Total Revenue:** The total money collected over a chosen period. It helps monitor the general financial health of the cinema.
* **Hall Occupancy Rate:** The percentage of filled seats compared to the total capacity of the room. It shows how well each room and movie schedule performs.
* **Revenue by Movie:** Shows how much money each movie makes. This is useful to check movie profitability and calculate payments for distributors.
* **Revenue by Show:** Shows the earnings for each specific showtime (afternoon, evening, early screenings) to help improve the schedule.

## Time Tracking {.unlisted .unnumbered}

For both Total Revenue and Number of Tickets Sold, you can filter data by selecting a start date and an end date. You can also view results by day, week, or month with a graph to identify seasonal trends and follow performance over time.

# Part 4 – Project management description

## Team organization

We are 4 people in the team and each one has a role for the whole project:

| Role | Person |
|---|---|
| Project Manager | Nolann |
| Technical Director | Simon |
| DAO Supervisor | Samuel |
| Testing Supervisor | Zoeb |

## Task assignment

We split the work mostly along these roles. Nolann handles coordination,
planning and keeping the Gantt diagram up to date. Simon takes care of the
technical side, meaning the architecture, the class diagram and the general
design choices. Samuel is more on the data side, so the database and the
data model, and how we access the data. And Zoeb is in charge of testing,
basically making sure stuff actually works before we call it done.

Of course this is not a strict separation: everyone can work on any part if
needed, especially since we're only 4 people. But these roles give each of
us a main area to focus on and to be responsible for.

## Methodology

We have a team meeting every week to check where everyone is, discuss
blocking points and decide what to do next. For now we mostly talk on
WhatsApp when we need to decide something quickly, and we put our documents
on Google Drive so everyone can access them. We know that WhatsApp is not the best communication tool for this sort of project work , so we're currently looking for a possibly more
efficient tool, but we haven't switched yet.

The code is on GitHub (github.com/nolannb35/ENSAI-2A-projet-info-team6), we
use it to keep track of the different parts of the project and work at the
same time without breaking each other's code.

We also want to do some kind of review before the big deadlines (Analysis
File, immersion, final delivery), just to check everyone's part actually
fits together before it's too late to fix.

## Gantt diagrams

### Phase 1: Analysis (28/08 - 17/09)

\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{gantt1.png}
\caption{Gantt chart for the analysis phase (28/08 - 17/09)}
\label{fig:gantt-phase1}
\end{figure}

This phase goes from the start of the project to the Analysis File
deadline. We start by understanding the subject and turning it into real
features, then we do the movie API benchmark at the same time as a first
draft of the technical design, and we finish by writing and reviewing the
report. The three TD meetings are basically checkpoints with our advisor,
where we can still adjust the plan if something's off.

### Phase 2: Development (17/09 - 21/11)

\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=1.15\textwidth]{gantt2.png}
\caption{Gantt chart for the development phase (17/09 - 21/11)}
\label{fig:gantt-phase2}
\end{figure}

This phase is where we actually code stuff. We start with the backend
(database, movie API, booking, payment, accounting), then the admin
back-office, and we finish with testing, updating the UML diagrams to
match what we actually coded, writing the final report and prepping the
defense. The 3-day immersion in early November is when we're expecting to
move a lot faster than usual since we'll have way more time on it. That's
basically it, everything ends up pointing to the final submission on
21/11.
